grades.quote: Programs that exhibit strong locality of reference will perform much better, not only because of the cache hierarchy, but also because of the TLB. The performance drop-off when your program exceeds the TLB’s capacity is generally quite precipitous.
grades.reason: Explains TLB pressure and limited TLB capacity. It says performance drops sharply when a program exceeds the TLB's reach, and that poor locality or sparse data structures hurt. This directly explains why page-sized strides in array access are slow: each access needs a new translation and causes TLB misses.

grades.quote: Most memory accesses will refer to page numbers present in the TLB, and so the MMU will be able to produce the corresponding page frame number without needing to access the page table.
grades.reason: Gives the underlying mechanism: translation needs a page table lookup unless the TLB holds the page, and the TLB relies on page-level locality. It implies that striding one page per access defeats the TLB and causes misses and extra page-table accesses. It doesn't explicitly discuss large strides or the performance cliff.
Bibliographic notes on page table variants and page replacement. Nothing about why page-strided array access is slow.
